headline: Light showers Sunday evening into Monday morning give way to a warming trend, with a much warmer Thanksgiving through Saturday (Friday highs likely 80 or more near the coast) and possible weak Santa Ana winds, while King Tides keep coastal flood alerts up on the Orange and San Diego County coasts through Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Sunday starts dry across coastal Carlsbad and the rest of San Diego County, with high clouds increasing and lower clouds (bases around 4,000–7,000 feet) filling in over the coast and valleys from about 10 AM; inland highs run 5 to 10 degrees below normal. A weak disturbance brings isolated to scattered light showers this evening into Monday morning from the mountains west to the coast, with the best coverage along the coast and in the San Diego County valleys, and showers could reach the Carlsbad and San Diego areas around 3 PM. Rain totals stay around 0.20 inch or less. Snow levels sit near 5,500–6,500 feet, but with so little moisture the mountains get a light dusting at most.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Showers end over Orange County and the Inland Empire around sunrise Monday but linger over San Diego County through mid-morning, then land areas dry out Monday afternoon. Tuesday turns warmer and drier with a light breeze blowing off the land, bringing highs near normal inland and about 3 to 5 degrees above normal near the coast. Wednesday looks similar, as a passing disturbance has trended much drier, with rain chances now under 10 percent.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving through Saturday will be much warmer as high pressure builds and winds blow offshore (from the land toward the sea), with the hottest day on Friday: there is a 60–80 percent chance of highs of 80 or more in the coastal areas and lower deserts, but no chance of 90 at this time. Offshore winds peak Thursday night into Friday morning, with a 45 percent chance of weak Santa Ana winds on Friday and a 25 percent chance of a weak-to-moderate event; about a quarter of computer model runs show a stronger system over Arizona and Mexico that would mean somewhat cooler weather but stronger offshore winds Thanksgiving. Saturday cools slightly as the winds turn back onshore, though highs stay 5 to 10 degrees above normal. Another storm could arrive late Saturday or next Sunday, but its timing and rain are very uncertain; for now it looks weak, with a 20–40 percent chance of a quarter inch or more from the coast to the mountains, and the national 8–14 day outlook leans slightly toward wetter-than-normal weather for early December.

coast: Morning high tides climb above 7 feet by Sunday and peak with King Tides on Wednesday, reaching 7.9–8.2 feet each morning Tuesday through Thursday (forecasters have raised the tide forecast above the usual predictions based on recent observations). A Coastal Flood Advisory covers the Orange County and San Diego County coasts from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM Tuesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Monday night through Thursday afternoon. Surf stays around 3–5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday afternoon into Thursday could push surf to 6–8 feet Thursday morning, locally up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches, on top of the high tides, though the swell forecast is still uncertain. Offshore, no marine hazards are expected through Tuesday, though a few showers may linger over the coastal waters into Monday afternoon; the next system and its swell could bring hazardous conditions Wednesday afternoon into Thursday, with gusts up to about 29 mph (25 knots) and seas of 8–12 feet, though its track and strength are uncertain.
watch_for: King Tides: Coastal Flood Advisory through 4 AM Tuesday, then a Coastal Flood Watch through Thursday afternoon, with morning tides near 8 feet and surf possibly 6–10 feet Thursday.
How strong the Thursday night–Friday offshore winds get (45% chance of weak Santa Ana winds Friday) and how hot Friday turns out.
Whether the late Saturday–Sunday storm brings meaningful rain.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in light Sunday-night showers and a dry, warmer Tuesday–Wednesday, certain that Thanksgiving through Saturday will be much warmer, but less sure how strong the offshore winds get and very uncertain about next weekend's storm.
